offers.name: Acer Aspire Lite 16" Laptop - Intel Core 5 120U - 16GB LPDDR5 - 512GB SSD - Windows 11 - Iron - Business/Student

praises: 16-inch WUXGA IPS at just 1.49 kg — the lightest big-screen laptop in this whole budget set
58Wh battery: users report a full class/workday away from the outlet
$899.99 flat with 16GB LPDDR5 undercuts the Aspire Go 16 twins
Two 20Gbps USB-C ports both do DP and 65W charging
16:10 1920x1200 panel gives real vertical workspace for documents
complaints: LPDDR5 soldered — 16GB is fixed forever despite the big chassis
Thin 'Lite' plastic feels cheaper than the Go line; deck flex and a light creaky lid
Dull ~45% NTSC IPS panel; colours flat for photo work
720p webcam, no IR face unlock, no keyboard backlight
Fan buzzes under sustained loads; the thin chassis has little thermal mass

standouts: Best big-screen portability in the dataset: 16" WUXGA IPS at 1.49 kg with a 58Wh battery
design_philosophy: The Aspire Lite 16 is Acer's thin-and-light budget trick: shave the plastic, solder the LPDDR5, and fit the biggest battery in the family (58Wh) into a 1.49 kg 16-inch shell at a flat $899.99. Everything that isn't visible — panel gamut, webcam, keyboard lighting, chassis rigidity — pays for that weight and runtime.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-aspire-go.md). Inferred from Core 5 120U Go 16 sibling: +1.3 battery (58.1 vs 51Wh verified), +1.2 portability (1.49 vs 1.65 kg verified), −0.3 build (thinner Lite shell), −2.0 upgradability (soldered LPDDR5 vs SO-DIMM). BBY lists 8 cores; Core 5 120U is a 10-core part — listed per Intel spec.
